o1.biggest_strength: It catches the main data signal and makes the paused 1-month break the centre of the new flow, with exact copy and solid build notes.
o1.biggest_mistake: It gives the 50% discount to switchers without evidence that this segment is price-sensitive or worth discounting, which risks repeating the old margin leak.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Remove or test-gate the switching-app discount, tighten the revenue math around discounted months, and keep every offer tied only to proven behaviour.

o2.biggest_strength: It makes the right strategic shift: bring back pause, stop blanket discounts, protect full-price trip returners, and treat lack of progress as a product fix.
o2.biggest_mistake: Some no-offer cards say or imply the cancellation is already complete before the user has tapped the visible cancel button, and the final legal note introduces an unneeded outside claim.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Clarify the no-offer copy so cancellation only happens after the button press, remove the speculative legal line, and add a sharper sprint build order.

reason: Both are strong and usable, but Output 2 is more disciplined with the money: it stops discounts entirely where the data does not prove they work. Output 1 is very build-ready, but the unsupported 50%-off offer for switchers is exactly the kind of margin leak this redesign should avoid.
